taxon.note: Scientific and common names as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit: a low spring herb with basal leaves and a leafless flowering stalk.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name; wcvp_names.csv of the v16 zip, read 2026-10-17).

traits.height_typical_m.note: FEIS species review, Erythronium grandiflorum (Fryer 2021): "Yellow avalanche-lily is a perennial herb that grows from 20 to 40 cm tall".

traits.life_span.note: FEIS species review, Erythronium grandiflorum (Fryer 2021): "a perennial herb".

traits.perennation.note: FEIS species review, Erythronium grandiflorum (Fryer 2021): "Yellow avalanche-lily has a corm and fibrous roots".

traits.rosette.note: FEIS species review, Erythronium grandiflorum (Fryer 2021): "Leaves are basal, from 5 to 20 cm long".

traits.leaf_habit.note: FEIS species review, Erythronium grandiflorum (Fryer 2021): "Plants die back in early summer and overwinter as corms".

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 427, Erythronium grandiflorum: "Leaves 7-15 cm. long, oblong-lanceolate, acute or acutish".

traits.leaf_apex.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 427, Erythronium grandiflorum: leaves "acute or acutish".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 427, Erythronium grandiflorum: "Leaves 7-15 cm. long"; FEIS (Fryer 2021): "from 5 to 20 cm long", kept as the rare extremes.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 427, Erythronium parviflorum: "Leaves oblong, gradually narrowed at both ends, 10-15 cm. long, 3-4 cm. wide"; set from 2 cm, as the photos show narrower leaves too.

traits.inflorescence.note: FEIS species review, Erythronium grandiflorum (Fryer 2021): "The inflorescence is a raceme; it is typically one-flowered but up to five-flowered".

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: FEIS species review, Erythronium grandiflorum (Fryer 2021): "typically one-flowered but up to five-flowered"; Abrams (1923 p. 427): "a solitary flower or often a raceme of 2-6 flowers".

traits.flower_posture.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 426, Erythronium: "Flowers large, nodding".

traits.perianth_reflexion.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 427, Erythronium grandiflorum: perianth-segments "strongly recurved"; of the subalpine plants (E. parviflorum, p. 427): "strongly reflexed".

traits.tepal_length_m.note: FNA vol. 26 (eFloras), Erythronium grandiflorum: tepals "recurved, bright yellow … narrowly ovate, 20–35 mm"; Abrams (1923 p. 427): perianth-segments "3-5 cm. long"; drawn 25 mm to 40 mm, the two floras' extremes kept as rare.

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: open flowers 4 cm to 6 cm across their strongly reflexed tepals, as in the photos.

traits.flower_colour.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 427, Erythronium grandiflorum: "perianth-segments bright yellow"; FEIS (Fryer 2021): "usually yellow but are sometimes white"; sRGB by eye.

traits.anther_colour.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 427, Erythronium parviflorum: "anthers cream color", as in the Rainier photos; Abrams's E. grandiflorum east of the Cascades has "anthers reddish purple".

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS species review, Erythronium grandiflorum (Fryer 2021): "The fruit is a capsule".

traits.flowering_months.note: FEIS species review, Erythronium grandiflorum (Fryer 2021): Table 2: flowers "April-July" (western Idaho), "May-July" (Intermountain region, Colorado), "early April-early May" (southeastern Washington); at Paradise it flowers in July as the snow melts ("usually at the edge of melting snowbanks").

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS species review, Erythronium grandiflorum (Fryer 2021): British Columbia: "fruits May-June at low elevations, July-August at high elevations".

generator.params.note: Yellow trout lily's (erythronium-americanum) values, changed by hand for glacier lily: two plain basal leaves under a leafless scape 20-40 cm tall (FEIS) with one or two nodding yellow flowers whose tepals curl right back. Not fitted to measurements.

appearance.organs.basal.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 427, Erythronium grandiflorum: "Leaves 7-15 cm. long, oblong-lanceolate", "narrowed to a broad and usually short petiole, not mottled". The template's mottling removed.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 427, Erythronium grandiflorum: "perianth-segments bright yellow lanceolate, acuminate, strongly recurved". Drawn bright yellow, the tepals curled well back.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: two plain green, lance-shaped basal leaves under a leafless stalk with one or two nodding, bright yellow lilies whose tepals sweep back. Organ cards from yellow trout lily's (erythronium-americanum), recoloured and resized by hand. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).

allometry.note: 0.28 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as it grows in subalpine parkland. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (2026-10-19): sizes and forms from Abrams and FEIS, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos, drawing values from a built-in template.
